messages:
maria: Hey — saw a spike where requests attributed to project A suddenly showed under service-account X during a quota surge. any ideas?
kevin: saw that too. looks like async claim handoff race between edge proxy and auth-exchange.
toni: is this the one where we fall back to projectless tokens? :thinking_face:
ankur: yeah — when exchange latency > 200ms the proxy stamps a fallback origin header and routing picks the fallback path.
maria: sample header from logs: `X-Redwood-Auth: sa=svc-alpha;orig=project;exchange_id=abc123` then later `X-Redwood-Auth: sa=svc-alpha;orig=none;exchange_id=`
olivia: ugh. so exchange clears exchange_id when it times out and that breaks attribution.
kevin: root problem: we mutate the request in two places (proxy and exchange). not idempotent.
toni: simple fix: add immutable origin_claim in the initial token, e.g. `origin_claim: org/<org>/proj/<proj>` and never overwrite.
ankur: +1 but that requires onboarding all existing tokens. migration headache.
maria: can we instead attach a signed exchange_token cookie that proxy can present back for late attribution?
kevin: might work. signed token = lightweight, proxy doesn't wait for exchange, and exchange can reconcile async.
olivia: telemetry note: we need a new metric for "attributed_vs_fallback_rate" and a tracer tag for exchange_roundtrip_ms.
sre-bot: alert created: "auth.attribution.fallback_rate" threshold=0.01 over 5m.
toni: UX: console shows per-key quota graphs. but if attribution flips later we end up charging wrong project on dashboard — loses trust. need reconciliation pipeline.
ankur: reconciliation pipeline idea: replay request traces from edge logs, re-run attribution with final exchange state, emit corrections to billing and dashboard.
maria: that could be eventual-consistent. billing might object.
olivia: product: we can show a "post-handoff corrections" badge and a reconciliation count in the console to be transparent.
kevin: low-risk rollout: 1) add signed exchange token header (no overwrite) 2) enable reconciliation in read-only mode (generate correction events but don't apply) 3) run canary on 5% traffic from orgs with active quotas 4) if good, enable corrections.
toni: code snippet for header we considered: ```
X-Redwood-Exchange: v1;id=abc123;sig=BASE64SIG
```
ankur: also consider quota policy: when exchange pending, we should provision temporary quota from org pool, not project. avoids accidental billing.
olivia: telemetry: create dashboard with panels: attribution_delay_p50/p95, fallback_rate_by_org, reconciliation_events. link to new dash: https://graf.redwood/d/attribution
sre-bot: created ticket INF-879: "reconciliation job + dashboards" assigned @ankur
kevin: concern: signed token can be replayed if long TTL. set TTL short (30s) and include nonce bound to request-id.
maria: security review needed for token format and KMS handling.
toni: ops: can we use existing sig key rotation scheme? devops-bot: rotation endpoint exists: `POST /kms/rotate?key=auth-exchange` (returns new_kid). will need client update.
ankur: final ask: can we get an infra canary this week? I'll start a PR for exchange token header and reconciliation consumer in read-only.
maria: ok — action items: ANKUR create PR, KEVIN define canary traffic slice, OLIVIA make dashboard, TONI security checklist, SREs monitor alert. thanks all :thumbsup:
